[{"state":"SMS exchange, 14 May

Oren O'Neill, contract desk: The notice from Larkspur Logistics asks us to correct the named remittance account on its executed service agreement. It does not dispute an amount, request a credit, or ask for a payment date. The agreement copy attached in the message lists the old account; the new account detail is on a signed amendment from both parties.

Viktor Petrov, intake clerk: I marked this BILLING because it mentions remittance and account. Please send it to the queue that handles charges, credits, and payment reconciliation.

Oren: That mark is not right. Our routing guide says amendments changing party details or terms go to contract administration; billing handles disputes about sums due, credits, and payment records. The signed amendment is the requested action here. No invoice or unpaid balance is referenced.

Viktor: Understood. I will forward the documents with the request to update the agreement record. There is no separate demand for money in the sender's message.","questions":[{"type":"binary","instruction":"Should this request be routed to the billing queue under the stated routing guide?","target":false,"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"The request updates an agreement using a signed amendment; the clerk's billing label conflicts with the guide."},{"type":"multiclass","instruction":"Which operational team should receive this matter based on the requested action and the routing guide?","candidates":[{"id":"billing","description":"Team resolving monetary account discrepancies, credits, and settlement records"},{"id":"contract_admin","description":"Team maintaining signed instruments and changes to party or term details"},{"id":"none","description":"No listed team fits the matter"}],"target":"contract_admin","hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"The signed change to agreement details falls under contract administration, not monetary reconciliation."}]},{"state":"Meeting notes, Foxglove Studio vendor review, 6 June

Leila Kaur presented a formal notice received from Meridian Software. It requests the outstanding annual platform fee of $4,800 under the signed license, and attaches the invoice and account ledger. Foxglove's ledger shows that this invoice remains unpaid; no credit or revised fee is requested. The notice does not allege breach of service terms or seek to change the license language.

Jonas Alvarez, meeting secretary, entered the action as LEGAL REVIEW, writing that any document called a formal notice must go to counsel. Leila checked the routing guide aloud: ordinary collection of an agreed, invoiced fee is handled by billing; counsel reviews alleged contractual breach, disputed interpretation, or proposed changes to legal terms. The group confirmed that the fee and invoice are not contested.

Decision recorded: send the payment request and ledger to the team responsible for account settlement. Keep the executed license in the file, but no contract interpretation is requested. The secretary's legal-review label is retained in the minutes as his initial classification, not as the agreed disposition.","questions":[{"type":"binary","instruction":"Should the notice be routed to counsel under the routing rule recorded in these meeting minutes?","target":false,"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"It seeks an uncontested invoiced fee; the minutes assign ordinary collection to billing, contrary to the secretary's label."},{"type":"multilabel","instruction":"Which functions should receive this matter under the routing guide, considering the action requested?","candidates":[{"id":"billing","description":"Team reconciling amounts owed and processing routine settlement requests"},{"id":"legal_review","description":"Counsel assessing alleged noncompliance or disputed meaning of legal terms"},{"id":"contract_admin","description":"Staff recording amendments to executed instruments"},{"id":"records_only","description":"Archive personnel with no action on payment or contract issues"}],"target":["billing"],"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"Only an undisputed invoice collection is requested; no breach, interpretation dispute, or amendment is involved."}]},{"state":"Incident postmortem, Bluefin Analytics, 21 July

A notice arrived from its equipment lessor, Larkspur Logistics, concerning the replacement-unit schedule in the signed lease. The sender asks to revise the delivery dates and substitute a different model; the notice does not bill for the equipment or claim any sum is overdue. The signed lease and the proposed schedule are attached. The operations log confirms no payment transaction or invoice was part of this incident.

Aiden Okafor, incident coordinator, wrote in the initial postmortem: “Route to billing: replacement model has a price, so this is a charge question.” That is his preliminary verdict. The routing guide distinguishes an actual request to settle or dispute a stated amount from a request to alter obligations in an executed agreement. The latter goes to contract administration, even if the changed terms may later affect cost.

During review, the team confirmed the lessor is asking for a change to delivery obligations and model specification, not asking Bluefin to pay or contest a fee. The postmortem keeps the coordinator's first label for audit history and records the requested next step as review of the proposed lease change.","questions":[{"type":"binary","instruction":"Should this incident be sent to the billing queue based on the request and the routing distinction?","target":false,"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"The lessor seeks changes to lease obligations, not settlement or dispute of an amount; the preliminary billing verdict is wrong."},{"type":"multiclass","instruction":"Which team should take the next action described in this postmortem, rather than rely on the initial label?","candidates":[{"id":"billing","description":"Group handling collection, settlement, and challenges to sums stated as due"},{"id":"contract_admin","description":"Group evaluating proposed revisions to obligations already recorded in a signed instrument"},{"id":"none","description":"No available group has responsibility for the requested action"}],"target":"contract_admin","hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"A proposed change to lease duties and specifications belongs with contract administration."}]},{"state":"SMS exchange, Jonas Mensah and intake desk, 3 August

Jonas: I received Bluefin Analytics' notice saying the service agreement ended on 31 July. It asks us to stop future service and confirms that no further monthly charges will be raised. The notice does not request repayment of earlier fees, adjustment of a current invoice, or any other credit. I am forwarding the signed termination notice for handling.

Intake desk: I tagged it BILLING because the message talks about monthly charges and stopping them. That seems enough for the accounts team.

Jonas: Please check the actual request. The routing card says accounts handles invoices, disputed sums, refunds, and credits. Contract administration handles termination notices and updates to the agreement register. This sender is not disputing a past charge; it is giving formal notice that the service relationship has ended, with the effective date stated above.

Intake desk: Agreed, the initial tag was not correct. I will send the notice to the team maintaining executed agreement records and ask them to record the end date. No payment action is requested in the SMS thread.","questions":[{"type":"binary","instruction":"Should this notice go to the billing queue according to the routing card and the request actually made?","target":false,"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"It gives formal termination notice and requests an agreement-register update; the initial billing tag is contradicted by the routing card."},{"type":"multilabel","instruction":"Which listed operational destinations are supported by the described request under the routing card?","candidates":[{"id":"agreement_records","description":"Team maintaining the register of signed arrangements and their end dates"},{"id":"invoice_settlement","description":"Team dealing with invoices, contested sums, and repayment adjustments"},{"id":"refunds_credits","description":"Team issuing money back or reducing an account balance"},{"id":"service_termination","description":"Team processing formal notice that an ongoing relationship is ending"}],"target":["agreement_records","service_termination"],"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"The notice ends the service relationship and requires recording the agreement end date; it requests no monetary adjustment."}]},{"state":"Meeting notes, Oren O'Neill / Foxglove Studio, 19 September

The parties reviewed a notice from Meridian Software about the wording of the confidentiality clause in their executed consulting contract. Meridian says the present clause is unclear and asks both sides to approve replacement language. It makes no demand for payment, fee reduction, refund, or invoice correction. The contract copy and proposed wording were circulated before the meeting.

Viktor Petrov, note taker, classified the item as BILLING, reasoning that a consulting contract usually has fees. The chair checked the written routing rule: questions about meaning of a clause or proposed changes to legal wording go to counsel; the billing desk handles account amounts and payment processing. The team agreed that this notice asks for legal wording review, not financial processing.

The minutes record the initial billing classification as an error and assign the proposed clause to the legal reviewer. No one reported an overdue balance, an invoice dispute, or a previously agreed fee change. The notice is therefore being routed by its stated request, rather than by the general fact that the contract has a commercial price.","questions":[{"type":"binary","instruction":"Should this matter be routed to counsel rather than the billing queue under the written rule?","target":true,"hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"The notice requests review and replacement of clause wording, which the rule assigns to counsel; the billing classification is wrong."},{"type":"multiclass","instruction":"Which destination is responsible for the specific work requested in these minutes?","candidates":[{"id":"billing","description":"Desk processing monetary account entries and payment matters"},{"id":"legal_counsel","description":"Reviewer addressing interpretation or revision of binding provisions"},{"id":"contract_admin","description":"Staff updating the register after an approved execution or termination"},{"id":"none","description":"No described destination covers this request"}],"target":"legal_counsel","hard_cases":["planted_verdict"],"notes":"The requested work is review of clause meaning and proposed legal wording, assigned to counsel."}]}]
